fields.description: Replace per-job workflow, attempt and event writes with bounded batch statements in the existing claim transaction. Preserve audit rows, workflow status guards, lease/resource fencing, claim origins and rollback. Add live regressions and run the repository verification script. Prioritize implementation; follow with a focused statement-count and RTT comparison.
fields.title: Batch job-claim audit and workflow writes

data.text: Implemented three batch side-effect statements in the existing claim transaction: one guarded workflow update and two INSERT SELECT writes from the already locked queue rows. Candidate/resource acquisition, leasing and commit error handling are unchanged. No public API or schema change; ADR-010 review finds no new consumer-controlled state transition or coordination obligation. Regenerated the three checked-query metadata entries with the repository SQLx 0.9.0 refresh tool against disposable PostgreSQL 18.6 and retained unrelated cache entries. Focused claim_batch_writes suite passed all 3 tests: four claim variants, 16/single/empty statement counts, audit identity and metadata, resource fences, workflow status/first-start guards and full rollback after each injected batch failure. Full scripts/verify.sh now running on pinned Rust 1.98.1.

Focused post-implementation measurement completed on Linux x86_64 / PostgreSQL 18.6. A temporary psycopg 3.3.6 probe executed old SQL from HEAD checked-query metadata and new SQL from generated metadata over a TCP delay proxy. Fixture: 16 claimed jobs, 8 workflow-linked; three warmup pairs then 12 alternating samples per version; timed only side effects, after leasing and before rollback. pg_stat_statements observed 48 versus 3 statements and exactly 40 row writes in both (8 workflow + 16 attempts + 16 events). Added RTT 0/2/5 ms gave calibrated SELECT 1 medians 0.31/2.60/5.41 ms and old/new medians 20.53/4.34, 132.06/16.51, 294.97/36.20 ms. This is a bounded SQL-phase probe, not end-to-end worker throughput or SQLx-driver evidence. Command: uv run --no-project --with psycopg[binary] python /tmp/batter-claim-mn9t/measure.py; local raw results /tmp/batter-claim-mn9t/measurement.json. Durable statement-count regression also observes the actual Rust public claim paths. No repository dependencies or migrations changed.

Final verification PASSED: bash scripts/verify.sh exited 0 on pinned Rust 1.98.1, Linux x86_64. It ran formatting, file budgets, all four Clippy configurations, all six matrix parts (workspace, no-default-features, doctests, consumers, runlimit, scripts), rustdoc and all five HTTP smoke profiles. Workspace test part passed in 428.681 seconds; copied-source Runledger and single-facade consumer checks also passed. Focused claim_batch_writes tests passed all 3 cases before the full run. Final git diff --check passed; Cargo.lock, migrations and public signatures remain unchanged, and canonical/postgres/runtime SQLx metadata agree. No semantic tests were relaxed, no local MSRV run, and no code commit or publication performed. Full verification log is /tmp/batter-claim-mn9t/verify.log; focused log is /tmp/batter-claim-mn9t/claim-tests.log. The disposable metadata/measurement PostgreSQL container was removed. Implementation, regression tests, native contract/changelog, status row, testing evidence and primary references are complete.
